items.q: A 32-year-old Ashkenazi Jewish woman presents with fatigue, splenomegaly, severe thrombocytopenia, and bone pain. Radiographs demonstrate an 'Erlenmeyer flask' deformity of the distal femur. Bone marrow biopsy reveals lipid-laden macrophages resembling 'wrinkled tissue paper'. Which condition is present?
items.exp: Gaucher disease is the most common lysosomal storage disorder, caused by beta-glucocerebrosidase deficiency. Glucosylceramide accumulates in macrophages (Gaucher cells with wrinkled paper cytoplasm), causing splenomegaly, pancytopenia, and bone crises.
r: Correct. Gaucher disease features wrinkled paper macrophages, bone crises, and splenomegaly.
Incorrect. Niemann-Pick cells are foamy histiocytes with sea-blue granules.
Incorrect. Tay-Sachs has no organomegaly or bone involvement.
Incorrect. Fabry disease presents with angiokeratomas and acroparesthesias.
items.kp: Gaucher disease is caused by beta-glucocerebrosidase deficiency; Gaucher macrophages with 'wrinkled tissue paper' cytoplasm cause bone crises, Erlenmeyer flask deformities, and splenomegaly.

items.q: A 6-month-old infant presents with developmental regression, exaggerated startle reflex to sound (hyperacusis), and progressive blindness. Fundoscopy demonstrates a bright cherry-red spot at the macula. Abdominal examination reveals NO hepatomegaly or splenomegaly. Which enzyme is deficient?
items.exp: Tay-Sachs disease is hexosaminidase A deficiency with GM2 ganglioside storage. Progressive neurodegeneration, hyperacusis, and macular cherry-red spot without hepatosplenomegaly are classic. In contrast, Niemann-Pick has prominent hepatosplenomegaly.
r: Correct. Tay-Sachs disease features cherry-red spot and neurodegeneration without hepatosplenomegaly.
Incorrect. Niemann-Pick disease features prominent hepatosplenomegaly.
Incorrect. Gaucher disease lacks cherry-red spot in Type 1.
Incorrect. Krabbe disease features globoid cells without macular cherry-red spot.
items.kp: Tay-Sachs disease (hexosaminidase A deficiency) presents with hyperacusis, neurodegeneration, and macular cherry-red spot without hepatosplenomegaly.

items.q: How does Niemann-Pick disease type A differ clinically from Tay-Sachs disease, despite both conditions presenting with a macular cherry-red spot in infancy?
o: Niemann-Pick features prominent hepatosplenomegaly and foamy histiocytes due to acid sphingomyelinase deficiency
Niemann-Pick features normal motor development throughout childhood
Tay-Sachs disease causes massive splenomegaly and portal hypertension
Tay-Sachs disease is inherited as an X-linked recessive trait
items.exp: Niemann-Pick type A (acid sphingomyelinase deficiency) accumulates sphingomyelin, causing foamy histiocytes, macular cherry-red spot, and massive hepatosplenomegaly. Tay-Sachs has identical macular appearance but normal liver/spleen size.
r: Correct. Niemann-Pick has prominent hepatosplenomegaly, unlike Tay-Sachs.
Incorrect. Both cause fatal early neurodegeneration.
Incorrect. Tay-Sachs has no splenomegaly.
Incorrect. Tay-Sachs is autosomal recessive.

items.q: A 12-year-old boy presents with severe burning pain in his hands and feet triggered by warm weather or exercise (acroparesthesias), clusters of non-blanching dark red maculopapules in the groin (angiokeratomas), and hypohidrosis. Which X-linked enzyme is deficient?
items.exp: Fabry disease is an X-linked recessive sphingolipidosis caused by alpha-galactosidase A deficiency. Globotriaosylceramide (Gb3 / ceramide trihexoside) accumulates in vascular endothelium, causing acroparesthesias, angiokeratomas, and progressive renal failure.
r: Correct. Fabry disease is X-linked alpha-galactosidase A deficiency with angiokeratomas and burning pain.
Incorrect. Metachromatic leukodystrophy causes demyelination without angiokeratomas.
Incorrect. Acid sphingomyelinase causes Niemann-Pick.
Incorrect. Beta-glucosidase causes Gaucher.
items.kp: Fabry disease is an X-linked recessive deficiency of alpha-galactosidase A, presenting with episodic acroparesthesias, angiokeratomas, hypohidrosis, and premature renal failure.

items.q: Krabbe disease (globoid cell leukodystrophy) is an autosomal recessive neurodegenerative disorder caused by deficiency of galactocerebrosidase. What toxic metabolite accumulates in oligodendrocytes, destroying myelin?
items.exp: Galactocerebrosidase deficiency prevents degradation of galactosylceramide and its deacylated derivative psychosine. Psychosine is highly cytotoxic to oligodendrocytes and Schwann cells, causing demyelination and globoid multinucleated macrophages.
r: Correct. Psychosine accumulation destroys myelin in Krabbe disease.
Incorrect. Glucosylceramide accumulates in Gaucher.
Incorrect. GM1 ganglioside accumulates in GM1 gangliosidosis.
Incorrect. Ceramide trihexoside accumulates in Fabry.

items.q: Metachromatic leukodystrophy is caused by deficiency of arylsulfatase A, leading to lysosomal accumulation of which sphingolipid that stains metachromatically with cresyl violet?
items.exp: Arylsulfatase A cleaves sulfate from cerebroside 3-sulfate. In metachromatic leukodystrophy, sulfatides accumulate in myelin-producing cells, shifting the absorption spectrum of cresyl violet dye (metachromasia) and causing central demyelination.
r: Correct. Arylsulfatase A deficiency causes sulfatide accumulation in metachromatic leukodystrophy.
Incorrect. Glucocerebroside accumulates in Gaucher.
Incorrect. Sphingomyelin accumulates in Niemann-Pick.
Incorrect. Gb3 accumulates in Fabry.

items.q: Which sphingolipid serves as the basic hydrophobic backbone for all cerebrosides, gangliosides, and sphingomyelin?
items.exp: Ceramide consists of sphingosine joined to a long-chain fatty acid via an amide linkage. Addition of phosphocholine yields sphingomyelin; addition of carbohydrate headgroups generates glycosphingolipids.
r: Correct. Ceramide is the common core precursor for all sphingolipids.
Incorrect. Sphinganine is an intermediate before ceramide formation.
Incorrect. Phosphatidylcholine is a glycerophospholipid.
Incorrect. Diacylglycerol has a glycerol backbone.

items.q: Miglustat and eliglustat are substrate reduction therapies approved for Gaucher disease type 1. What enzyme do they inhibit to reduce glucosylceramide synthesis?
items.exp: Miglustat and eliglustat are substrate reduction agents that competitively inhibit glucosylceramide synthase, decreasing the cellular rate of glucosylceramide production to match residual clearance capacity.
r: Correct. They inhibit glucosylceramide synthase to reduce substrate load.
Incorrect. Glucocerebrosidase is the deficient enzyme.
Incorrect. Acid ceramidase cleaves ceramide in Farber disease.
Incorrect. Sphingomyelin synthase makes sphingomyelin.

items.q: Farber lipogranulomatosis is a rare lysosomal disorder characterized by painful subcutaneous nodules, joint contractures, and hoarseness due to laryngeal involvement. Which enzyme is deficient?
items.exp: Farber disease is caused by acid ceramidase deficiency, leading to ceramide accumulation in lysosomes throughout connective tissue and granuloma formation in joints, larynx, and subcutaneous tissues.
r: Correct. Acid ceramidase deficiency causes Farber lipogranulomatosis with painful nodules and hoarseness.
Incorrect. Galactocerebrosidase causes Krabbe.
Incorrect. Arylsulfatase A causes metachromatic leukodystrophy.
Incorrect. Hexosaminidase B deficiency causes Sandhoff disease.

items.q: Niemann-Pick disease type C (NPC) differs fundamentally from types A and B because the underlying defect involves which non-enzymatic cellular process?
o: Defective intracellular trafficking and unesterified cholesterol export from lysosomes (NPC1 / NPC2 mutations)
Primary enzymatic deficiency of acid sphingomyelinase
Defective endosomal acidification by V-type ATPase
items.exp: Niemann-Pick type C is caused by mutations in NPC1 or NPC2, which encode lysosomal cholesterol export proteins. Cholesterol and glycolipids become trapped in lysosomes, causing vertical supranuclear gaze palsy, ataxia, and dementia.
r: Correct. NPC involves defective NPC1/NPC2 lysosomal cholesterol trafficking, not sphingomyelinase deficiency.
Incorrect. Acid sphingomyelinase deficiency causes Niemann-Pick types A and B.
Incorrect. V-type ATPase is unaffected.
Incorrect. Glycosylation is intact.
